correctness.rationale: The normal-fan/Hasse facet dictionary is verified from PRW Prop. 3.5(8), and toric degree counts facets of the vertex normal cone. The A/B run partition is bijective with acyclic orientations, and each run contributes L-1 internal covers plus its oriented sinks or sources as surviving spokes. The switch-string bijection gives binom(L,2s-1); summing all compositions yields the displayed rational formal power series. Excess zero exactly means a tree of Hasse edges whose root differences form a unimodular integral basis, so fixed-point smoothness is proved in every characteristic. Finite exhaustive checker independently checks full degree histograms m=1..8 and path sink counts L=1..10; and global f1 counts via edge contractions m=1..7; these do not substitute for the symbolic infinite proof. The invariant is expressly NOT local divisor-class rank, a potentially incorrect conflation.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A wheel adds a closing rim edge and is a different family; the theta family has disjoint internal arms and does not contain general overlapping-triangle fans; complete-multipartite smoothness covers small cases only and no general m≥4 fan. The present invariant is number of normal-cone FACETS minus dimension (equivalently polytope vertex-degree excess), not number of normal-cone rays or the local class-group rank, so adjacent literature on divisor classes cannot subsume it by a mistaken identification. value.rationale: The parameterized family fan K1∨P_m has a natural toric interpretation and changes from fully simple low-dimensional members to generally nonsimple ones. Vertex-degree excess measures how many torus-invariant curves beyond dimension pass through each fixed point, giving a first structural local smoothness obstruction. Exact all-degree frequencies, a Fibonacci smooth count, and closed moment formulas for the whole infinite family are meaningful beyond global face counts or isolated low-dimensional computations; the run mechanism explains their persistence.
